title: Colorado PUC Decision R26-0098: Recommended Decision Granting Motion to Dismiss Formal Complaint and Closing Proceeding
summary: Recommended Decision Granting Motion to Dismiss Formal Complaint and Closing Proceeding
text:
Decision No. R26-0098 
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF COLORADO 
PROCEEDING NO. 25F-0530EG 
CHARLES RITTENHOUSE, 
COMPLAINANT, 
V. 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY OF COLORADO, 
RESPONDENT. 
RECOMMENDED DECISION GRANTING MOTION TO 
DISMISS FORMAL COMPLAINT AND CLOSING 
PROCEEDING 
Issued Date: February 12, 2026 
I. 
PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND 
1. 
On December 18, 2025, Charles Rittenhouse (“Complainant” or “Mr. 
Rittenhouse”) filed with the Colorado Public Utilities Commission (“Commission”) a Formal 
Complaint (“Complaint”) against Public Service Company of Colorado (“Public Service,” 
“Respondent,” or the “Company”).1 
2. 
On December 22, 2025, the Commission Director (“Director”) issued an Order to 
Satisfy or Answer, directing Respondent to either satisfy the matters raised in the Complaint or 

1 The Complaint identified “XCEL ENERGY” as the Respondent in the Complaint. However, 
Public Service Company of Colorado conducts utility operations in Colorado as a wholly-owned subsidiary 
of Xcel Energy Inc., a public utility holding company. Accordingly, Public Service is the proper designation 
for the Respondent in this matter.

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0098

2 
file a written answer within 20 days of service of the Order. The Director also issued an Order 
Setting Hearing and Notice of Hearing, scheduling a hearing in this matter before an 
Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) on March 9, 2026. 
3. 
By Decision No. R26-0015-I, issued January 8, 2026, the evidentiary hearing in 
this Proceeding was rescheduled for March 13, 2026. 
4. 
On January 12, 2026, Public Service Company of Colorado’s Motion to Dismiss 
Formal Complaint with Prejudice (“Motion”) was filed by the Company. 
5. 
No response to the Motion was filed. 
II. 
JURISDICTION AND RELEVANT LAW 
6. 
The Commission has jurisdiction over Public Service as a public utility and over 
this formal complaint proceeding pursuant to §§ 40-1-103, 40-6-108, and 40-6-109, C.R.S. 
7. 
Rule 1302(a) of the Rules of Practice and Procedure, 4 Code of Colorado 
Regulations (“CCR”) 723-1, requires that a formal complaint “shall set forth sufficient facts and 
information to adequately advise the respondent and the Commission of the relief sought and, if 
known, how any statute, rule, tariff, price list, time schedule, decision, or agreement memorialized, 
accepted, or approved by Commission decision is alleged to have been violated.” 
8. 
Rule 1308(e) of the Rules of Practice and Procedure, 4 CCR 723-1, permits a 
respondent to file a motion to dismiss a complaint prior to filing an answer. 
9. 
In evaluating a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim upon which relief can 
be granted, the Commission accepts as true all well-pleaded factual allegations in the complaint 
and views them in the light most favorable to the complainant. Dismissal is appropriate only where 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0098 
Proceeding No. 25F-0530EG 
3 
the complaint fails to allege facts that, if proven, would entitle the complainant to relief under any 
applicable statute, rule, tariff, or Commission decision. 2 
10. 
Rule 3664(b) of the Rules Regulating Electric Utilities, 4 CCR 723-3, governs the 
treatment of excess electricity produced by a customer with retail renewable distributed generation. 
The rule provides that excess kilowatt-hour (“kWh”) credits “shall be carried forward from month 
to month and credited at a ratio of 1:1 against the customer’s retail kWh consumption in subsequent 
months,” and further provides for compensation of accrued excess credits within specified 
timeframes at the investor-owned qualifying retail utility’s average hourly incremental cost, 
subject to a one-time election to roll over credits indefinitely. 
III. 
FINDINGS OF FACT, ANALYSIS, AND CONCLUSIONS 
11. 
The Complaint concerns an alleged “billing dispute for solar power credits totaling 
$2906.78 as of 18 December 2025.”3 
12. 
The Complaint requests that the Complainant be permitted to use those credits to 
pay the “entire Xcel energy bill (including gas charges),” or alternatively receive a “refund.”4 
13. 
The Complaint further states: “I believe PUC should intervene and regulate this 
matter as Xcel’s behavior is abusive and punitive.”5 
14. 
The Motion seeks dismissal of the Complaint for failure to state a claim upon which 
relief can be granted, asserting that the relief requested is inconsistent with Rule 3664(b) and the 
Company’s Commission-approved electric tariff. The Motion states in relevant part: 
…the Complaint requests a treatment of excess energy which is inconsistent 
with applicable Commission Rule or the Public Service Electric Tariff, and 

2 Rules 1302(a) and 1308(e) of the Rules of Practice and Procedure, 4 CCR 723-1; see also § 40-
6-108, C.R.S. 
3 Complaint at p. 1. 
4 Id. 
5 Id. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0098 
Proceeding No. 25F-0530EG 
4 
which would actually violate the law if the value of excess electricity were 
applied to natural gas charges. 
*** 
… Rule 3664(b) first provides that excess electricity must be carried 
forward to future months and credited against future consumption. As such, 
it would be impermissible for Public Service to apply the value of such 
excess electricity to a customer’s natural gas bill. To do so would violate 
Rule 3664(b) as well as the underlying statute, § 40-2-124(1)(e)(I)(B), 
C.R.S. For this reason, it would be illegal to apply the value of excess 
electricity produced by Complainant’s retail renewable distributed 
generation resource to Complainant’s natural gas charges. 
After setting forth that excess electricity must be carried forward to future 
months and credited against future consumption, Rule 3664(b) provides two 
options for accrued excess electricity. Either excess electricity may be paid 
out to the customer at the end of each calendar year at the average hourly 
incremental cost of electricity (“AHIC”), or the customer may make a one-
time election for excess electricity to be rolled over from month to month 
indefinitely until the customer terminates service, at which time no payment 
is required for remaining excess electricity. Importantly, end of year 
payment at AHIC is not a “refund” as it represents only a portion of the cost 
of providing electricity to customers and is thus much less valuable than the 
value of the credit against future consumption. Moreover, end of year 
payment at AHIC is not required after a customer has chosen to roll over 
excess electricity produced by a retail renewable distributed generation 
resource from month to month indefinitely. Therefore, Public Service is not 
required to “refund” the value of excess electricity produced by 
Complainant’s retail renewable distributed generation resource, or even to 
pay the much lower AHIC value, following years of gradual accrual of 
excess electricity. 
The Public Service Electric Tariff incorporates the key applicable 
provisions of Rule 3664(b) at Sheets 112D and 112E. Thus, as with the case 
of Rule 3664(b), under the Commission-approved Public Service Electric 
Tariff, it would be impermissible for Public Service to apply the value of 
such excess electricity to a customer’s natural gas bill or for Public Service 
to “refund” the value of excess electricity produced by a customer’s retail 
renewable distributed generation resource. 
The Complaint does not allege that Public Service has committed an act or 
omission inconsistent with law; instead, it requests treatment of excess 
energy in violation of Commission Rule and the Public Service Electric 
Tariff. Because the applicable Commission Rule and Public Service Electric 
Tariff do not require or permit the value of excess electricity produced by a 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0098 
Proceeding No. 25F-0530EG 
5 
customer’s retail renewable distributed generation resource to be applied to 
natural gas charges or “refunded,” the Company declining to do so could 
not constitute “abusive and punitive” behavior. The Commission has 
already considered the topic of excess electricity produced by a retail 
renewable distributed generation resource and promulgated Rule 3664(b) 
governing the treatment of excess electricity. For these reasons, this is not 
a claim upon which relief can be granted.6 
15. 
By its plain terms, Rule 3664(b) requires that excess kWh credits be carried forward 
from month to month and credited at a 1:1 ratio against future retail kWh consumption. The rule 
does not require a utility to apply excess electric credits to natural gas service charges. 
16. 
Commission-approved tariffs implementing Rule 3664(b), including Public 
Service’s Colorado PUC No. 8, Sheets 112D–112E, must conform to applicable statutes and 
Commission rules, and the Commission may not grant relief in an adjudicatory complaint 
proceeding that is contrary to those governing statutory, rule, or tariff requirements.7 
17. 
The Complaint does not allege facts that, if proven, would demonstrate that the 
Respondent has failed to carry forward excess kWh credits from month to month, failed to apply 
those credits against future retail kWh consumption, failed to comply with the year-end or 
termination-of-service compensation provisions of Rule 3664(b), or otherwise violated a 
Commission rule, tariff, or decision. Instead, the Complaint requests relief that is inconsistent with 
the treatment of excess credits set forth in Rule 3664(b), as summarized above. 
18. 
Under Rule 1302(a), the Complaint must provide sufficient facts and information 
to advise the Respondent and the Commission of the relief sought and, if known, how a statute, 
rule, or tariff is alleged to have been violated. The Complaint, as pleaded, does not identify a 
violation of a statute, rule, or tariff; it instead seeks a change in how excess credits are applied 

6 Id. 
7 See § 40-2-124, C.R.S.; Rule 3664(b) of the Rules Regulating Electric Utilities, 4 CCR 723-3; 
Public Service Company of Colorado Electric Tariff, Colorado PUC No. 8, Sheets 112D–112E. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. R26-0098 
Proceeding No. 25F-0530EG 
6 
(including application to gas charges or an immediate refund) that is not supported by Rule 
3664(b). 
19. 
Therefore, even accepting the Complaint’s well-pleaded factual allegations as true, 
the Complaint fails to state a claim upon which relief can be granted under any applicable statute, 
Commission rule, or Commission-approved tariff. Accordingly, dismissal is appropriate pursuant 
to Rule 1308(e). 
20. 
Public Service requests dismissal with prejudice. Since the relief sought in the 
Complaint is contrary to Rule 3664(b), and is therefore unavailable as a matter of law, the 
Complaint is dismissed with prejudice because relief is legally unavailable. Accordingly, 
amendment of the Complaint would be futile, and dismissal with prejudice is appropriate under 
Rule 1308(e). 
21. 
Nothing in this Recommended Decision precludes the Complainant from filing a 
future complaint that is consistent with Rule 3664(b), and alleges facts which, if proven, would 
demonstrate a violation of an applicable statute, Commission rule, tariff, or decision. The dismissal 
with prejudice applies only to the relief requested in the Complaint, which, as explained above, is 
legally unavailable as a matter of law. 
IV. 
EVIDENTIARY HEARING 
22. 
Given the dismissal of the Complaint herein, further litigation is no longer 
necessary. Therefore, the evidentiary hearing in this Proceeding will be vacated, and this 
Proceeding will be closed, as ordered below.

V. 
TRANSMISSION OF THE RECORD 
23. 
Pursuant to § 40-6-109(2), C.R.S., the ALJ transmits to the Commission the record 
and exhibits in this proceeding together with this written Recommended Decision, which contains 
findings of fact and conclusions thereon, together with the recommended order. 
VI. 
ORDER 
The Commission Orders That: 
24. 
Consistent with the discussion above, the above-captioned Complaint, filed by 
Charles Rittenhouse on December 18, 2025, is dismissed with prejudice. 
25. 
The evidentiary hearing scheduled for March 13, 2026, is vacated. 
26. 
Proceeding No. 25F-0530EG is closed. 
27. 
This Recommended Decision shall be effective on the date it becomes the Decision 
of the Commission, if that is the case, and is entered as of the date above. As provided by § 40-6-
109, C.R.S., copies of this Recommended Decision shall be served upon the parties who may file 
exceptions to it. 

a. If no exceptions are filed within 20 days after service or within any extended 
period of time authorized, or unless the recommended decision is stayed by 
the Commission upon its own motion, the recommended decision shall 
become the decision of the Commission and subject to the provisions of 
§ 40-6-114, C.R.S. 
b. If a party seeks to amend, modify, annul, or reverse basic findings of fact in 
its exceptions, that party must request and pay for a transcript to be filed, or 
the parties may stipulate to portions of the transcript according to the 
procedure stated in § 40-6-113, C.R.S. If no transcript or stipulation is filed, 
the Commission is bound by the facts set out by the administrative law judge 
and the parties cannot challenge these facts. This will limit what the 
Commission can review if exceptions are filed.
